newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Thin interest in Vietnam's rice, despite discount.
newsitem.headline: Thin interest in Vietnam's rice, despite discount.

text.p: Vietnam's export rice market has continued very quiet this week as buyers look to other sources, including Pakistan, for cheaper supplies, traders said on Thursday.
Eight vessels were currently in Saigon, with shipments bound for Iran, Cuba, Europe, South Africa and North Korea.
Dealers said agents for Pyongyang, which is facing an acute domestic food shortage, had been looking for some 9,000 tonnes of rice from Vietnam and a similar quantity from Thailand.
Vietnam's rice trade has been quiet for more than a month.
Dealers said discounts were now being offered against a nominal price for five percent broken of $280 per tonne FOB Saigon, unchanged from a week ago.
However, they said there were few takers.
"Shippers are willing to discount by $6-$7 per tonne, but people are nervous to book Vietnamese because they're discounting and you never know what will happen," one said.
Vietnam's domestic market is currently dominated by demand from northern areas of the country which have been hit badly this year by flooding and storms.
